reviews.text: Overall a decent place to check out if you are into the arts scene. Do note however that the layout can be slightly confusing and the signs around aren’t very helpful. Toilets are nothing compared to the western style ones and you need to come prepared with your own tissue paper.
Great spot for vintage shopping, coffee, and craft beer. There’s a very cool NBeer pub in a train car.
Great place . Loads of interesting contemporary Art and industrial grunge. Go there. It's really big so pre plan
The place is large and well-organized, with many artworks displayed. Some of them required payment for entrance. The atmosphere was nice. It was one of my favorite places during this visit.

Overall a positive experience but some areas could see some improvements. 1. Bathrooms should have more western style toilets 2. Better maps and road signage for the area district. We like the variety of shopping and exhibitions. We were a bit disappointed when some of the exhibits were closed. We did enjoy the Jingdong soap museum.

‘A surprising art section in Beijing’ Without any expectations, I decided to visit 798 Art zone. I was positively surprised how spacious it was and how many art galleries you could find. You can feel the influence on the architecture from post war Europe in the art zone. I definitely enjoyed feeling like I was walking in Europe. The only thing to keep in mind that it is not east to reach by public transportation and it can take a long time to find a taxi!

One of my favorite places to visit in Beijing! Great for one of a kind souvenirs. As a westerner, it is good to have a local along to give knowledge of many historical or popular culture references in the art. A few high end galleries exist, but mostly it is a collection of indie artist stores for jewelry, clothing, glass, carvings, pottery and myriad other items. The area is huge, so you will not see everything in a single day. Just relax and see what interests you in the stores, galleries, restaurants or in the streets. It is a lot to absorb. I had no trouble finding 798 having come by ride share and public transportation several times. Note: prices here are higher than elsewhere in Beijing, but not outrageous. Think Sanlitun.

The entire art district spans over a really large plot of land. For those of you that may enjoy visiting galleries here, there are a very large number of galleries available. Most are free to visit so you may take the time to slowly browse the location. For those of us that are not so interested in art, there are also alot of cafe's and restaurants that you are able to visit. Furthermore, the grungy vibe that the location has, would provide a good variety of instagrammable backdrops for you to take some photos. I would give myself at least 1.5 hours here.

A nice escape from the hustle and bustle of Beijing. The area is free to access and is dotted with beautiful wall art, graffiti, and modern art museums. Most of the museums are free while some require a small entrance fee. Although it takes about an hour to get to from the city center, it's a breath of fresh air to see a blend of Western and Chinese artwork and decor. There are little handicraft, DIY shops, and a plethora of modern cafes for you to sit and enjoy a tea or coffee in. Make sure to take the time to explore the area thoroughly as it's broken up into multiple art zones and doesn't just consist of the 798.

Its a very big area full of art of all sorts. Graffiti, contemporary, abstract, tech stuff, you name it. Its very hard to visit each showcase because its massive. But definitely worth your while. Also plenty of cafés. It can get crowded during the weekends or when there is a festival. Plenty of shops too. Definitely artsy

This is a great spot for tourists looking for mini souvenirs for family. Also cool art galleries, cafes, drinks, and music shops. This area is highly dedicated to artist and creative beings. Love this artisan area!

The 798 Art Zone in Beijing is a dynamic blend of art, culture, and history. Explore its industrial-chic spaces filled with galleries, studios, and cafés, offering a unique glimpse into China's thriving contemporary art scene. A must-visit for art enthusiasts!

This area of Beijing is full of artists studios, unique shops and coffeehouses. It was an old army base that has very unique buildings with graffiti and art everywhere. Take some time to explore the area. If you are an instagrammer, you will have no shortage of places to take photos.
Chatming huge Art Zone converted from Industrial factory areas. Plenty of gallery, eye-catching facde, architecture, alleys, cafes and restaurants. Totally worth visiting while Beijing.

This is an abandoned industrial area that is now converted into an art district. There are murals, wall arts, sculptures, graffiti all over this area. The eateries and small coffee shops make this place unique and happening that any art lover will love to visit and experience the atmosphere. I spent several hours appreciating the art and had pizza at Lakers Pizza which was delicious. An enchanting place that every art lover should not miss if in Beijing.

The Art Zone is a place full of all the kinds of art you won’t see in the rest of the Capital. Alternative, abstract, modern, often even absurd. In some cases you might even see exhibits that you will consider whether they are “art” or not. However, beauty is in the eye of the beholder, so I definitely recommend you visit the Art Zone and explore it yourself. Keep in mind that many exhibitions have an entrance fee. Also it might be difficult to navigate around, as things aren’t as straightforward as in the rest of Beijing and many exhibitions change from time to time.

New regional mark of the city. Galleries, design studios, art exhibition spaces, artists' studios, fashionable shops, restaurants, bars etc assemble here. 798 Art district is open for free, but some galleries and exhibition halls sell admission tickets.Opening HoursThe art district is open all day long. Most shops and galleries inside are open from 10:00 to 18:00 and some may close on Monday.

Often called ground zero for hipsters in Beijing, the Art District is eye opening, especially if you're looking for breadth in your experience of the city. Excellent range of cuisine, particularly reminiscent of the Melbourne café scene, it offers to the mix varieties of art galleries, record stores, plant stores with cacti and succulents, micro-breweries, calligraphy.... Like i said, hipster central, but in the best possible way.
The most unique and wonderful place I stumbled across in Beijing! Reached at night so most of the galleries we're shut.. but the artwork was still breathtaking!

Absolutely authentic place for China. A huge territory with lots of shops, art galleries, cafes. Best place for creative people to get some inspiration, community and take a lot of pictures. That’s definitely a place for many video and photo shootings.

Beijing 798 art zone is something similar to the Shanghai M50 art enclave. The place is bigger than the M50 art zone also its famous because many international Art festivals were conducted here and hence the place is really famous among the foreign tourist. Most of the halls or shops as you can say are free to public for viewing and are available for purchase. To get to the Beijing art zone it’s a long way from the nearby subway station and we took a small electric tuk tuk to reach there for RMB 20/-

Perfect area to spend a day. Multiple restaurants and also you can find cuisines from different nations. Walls with graffiti, structure is like an abandoned industrial area which was later converted to commercialisation. You can go there in groups but must go at-least once.
Step back in time and enjoy many hours walking around the zone, see the many creative artists and buy some great works of art. Some cafes to have a rest and enjoy a nice coffee and some lunch
Recommended, probably one of the coolest places to visit in the "new" Beijing. Plenty of Art galleries, nice restaurants and street art
spent 3 hrs at here! i had so much fun strolling around. if you go there by bus, you can stop at 北京电机总厂(bei jing dian ji zong chang) only the bus number 405 and 593 that goes to this station.
Amazing place in Beijing. An old manufacturing district that has been taken over by the avantguard artist. Walkable area! A little bit complicated to access by subway or bus. Go see it!

A nice place to spend an afternoon strolling, checking out some galleries and grabbing a coffee or an ice cream. Nothing avant garde here, but worth a visit. Most galleries are free, some have a fee. The people watching is almost as good as the art.

A must visit when you're in Beijing. Avoid taking kids as they might not enjoy the idea. Be ready to spend at least half a day. Have a leisurely stroll and enjoy the old industrial area converted to art zone.

A bohemian, artistic, cultural hotspot in north-east Beijing. Art galleries, street art, sculpture, cafes and restaurants, abound in this old industrial zone revamped into a hip art zone for artists. Great place to stroll around, enjoying the laid back vibe and must visit if in the area.

Slightly overrated in my view and over commercialized. Many of the exhibition requires payment to access (which is fair) but the quality was, in my personal assessment, quite lacking. Street art was somewhat interesting but these were not frequently seen and most of those gave off a plasticky mass produced feel. Still could be a worthwhile trip if you're looking for something different. Not very accessible by train though - I took a cab.

Totally worth the visit as a main tourist destination to better understand the contempory art scene in Beijing. There is interesting sculpture and art every few meters as you walk from gallery to gallery. The Zhao Bandi China Party exhibit at UCCA is phenomenal and a must-see as he uses whimsy to comment on class in society. I will be thinking about what I saw in the 798 for a long time.
Cool place to hang out and experience the local art community. Lots of one off stores and cafes. Can definitely spend an entire day here.
Absolutely amazing district that showcases some very cool art pieces. Lots of different galleries to take a look at and enjoy.

Occupying what once an industrial complex of buildings etc., this art distric offers an alternative to the traditional art museum experience, and provides a great way to appreciate and support local talent. There are maps available as you walk around, but they aren't always as helpful for English speakers as they could be. Good place if you want a quite coffee house (there are plenty abound) to sit and read or work too.
"Underrated" One of the best non-tourists spots in Beijing with amazing exhibits and many contemporary galleries from a wide variety of artists.
Great area of Beijing, stayed at the Gracie Art Hotel which is also very cool, lots of nice restaurant and bar around.
A must see in Beijing. Huge creative scene wirh nice coffees interesing galleries and good art.
We enjoyed our little hike in the art zone. Beautiful elements on the street and nice shops. And enough choice to have lunch.

This is a must visit for art lover..we can spend few hours walking around to explore..it characterized by modern chinese culture, the world famous cultural and creative industries centralized area.. There are mural, wall arts, statues, sculptures ,galleries, souvenir shops, old industrial, thematic house, etc.. I recommend you to go with friends with same interest to enjoy your time here..
A large area with lots of art galleries, some are free others are paid. There are also many cafes and shops/boutiques
Very nice precinct. Great to walk around and get a coffee sitting in the street or courtyard

Looking for the art culture place in Beijing, here you are !! Do not run, do not follow a track,.. get lost in this old industrial Parc .. Special tip for Shenji restaurant .. local food by friendly people !

The quality of the art is not even close to what you see in art museums and galleries in Beijing and Shanghai. It's a great place to shop though. I picked up some beautiful earrings for about $20 USD each. Similar to the picture.

Creative and imaginative art district in Beijing. One of the highlights people should visit in Beijing. Many galleries, cafes and shops to explore. The area is quite big with many lanes to visit. Definitely bring your camera to get some good pictures

A very enjoyable and hip area in Beijing to walk around. We didn't go with a plan and just ended up meandering around and into different galleries. There were some interesting artists displaying work and a large number of public statues and graffiti art. Lots of coffee shops for a rest or hot drink. Was a nice contrast to some of the more historical sites to see a more contemporary part of the city.

It's a very interesting place to go though quite confusing. It's got very interesting arts stuff ranging from graffiti's in some alleys, to statues around to the actual galleries. They have many shops selling interesting clothing or antiques. Great restaurants and cafes all around. It will take an entire day to explore everything, all the alleys. It's a very fun and great place to see.
Visited this Artistic area during Winter. Definitely a place people shouldn’t give a miss when in Beijing!
Wonderful place to pay a visit, besides galleries there are many shops selling interesting stuff.

For those who give bad rank, they have a reason: The place used to be more vibrant and active (in the 90's and 00's), but now it's much emptier and boring... You walk endlessly across the large streets to small corridors, waiting to be surprised... then what? You've already finished! Maybe the best galleries already moved to better locations in downtown, which explains why.

Great art ❣️ Food not so good 👎 if you like art galleries and stuff then this is a place for you. You can go and see galleries, museums, street art, graffiti walls. Buy some good stuff like vessels, show pieces, jewellery, rings etc. It's a good place to spend a day.

Always top of my list for family and friends visiting me in Beijing. Great sculptures, galleries and street art, with tons of events and a diverse crowd. It's huge so don't expect to see everything in one sitting, but there at restaurants, shops and stalls dotted around.

798 used to be an old industrial area. During the last decade it has evolved into one of the most inspiring areas in Beijing. It features a range of galleries and coffee shops and are often used used as the go to place for big cultural events like fashion shows. Brand promotions etc. You can spend a lot of time exploring the area.

I visited here one day on my student exchange trip in 2012. I meet a sweet artist who makes serene watercolor paintings. He had visited my hometown when he was younger. The shops all around were pleasing to be in. The sights were all pleasing to take in. I yearn to go back <3

A fantastic vibrant art area. Housed in 1950s East German factories, 798 offers a wide selection of art galleries, cafés, bars and shops for people to enjoy. Some galleries do require a small fee and contain art from around the world. There is alot to see and do so give your self at least half a day to see it all. The venue is always changing thus making each visit slightly different from the last. Accessible by metro, bus and taxi.

We have been here with a delegation . After several days in China we were really happy to visit this Bavarian pub . German Food and german Beer, mixed with Live music . Had a lot of fun that evening and highly recommend this location.
Amazing place, must visit again. It is a great idea of the concept of using old buildings from some factory or whatever and making it an art district

I would give Zero star if I can. I was threatened by a soap shop owner inside 798 Art zone. The owner wasn’t happy that HK people went inside her shop, then she call her husband and brother to come. I had been put under home arrested. When her brother arrived, he chokehold me. I was scared and couldn’t breathed then I bite his arm and he said, “she hurts me now, call police.” When the police arrived, I request to go hospital and have assessment because of chokehold, but police refused and said, “they report you hurt them, perpetrator can’t request anything.” When I arrived police station, I was asked to pay USD$900 by a China police sergeant. I was shocked of the corruption between the shop and police and I refused to pay any money. Luckily, some of friends were lawyers and reporters in Beijing. I called them secretly for help. The police kept me for 1 night 2 days detention and threatened me “no pay no release”. Finally, the police didn’t charge me any crime and released me. It’s terrible experience in 798 Art zone.

Amazing place where artist and art lover meet, lots of visual art gallery and live music. A really nice place for students to learn about contemporary art or just to hangout and enjoy your coffee or tea. I really want to live there, enjoy the atmosphere more, and be one of them. Too bad i have to go back home. Thank for bringing me there Yufei and Enjuen.

Your experience would really depend on what you seek. If you are one of average person who isn’t so literate on Art, and just want to hang out at cafes, or look for a cool & chic location for selfie/portraits, then there are enough places to enjoy and explore. For those who are a serious Art person, this might be a little disappointing.
Graffitis, art works, murals, statues, souvenirs... Everywhere... I am an artist want to be, so I had a great time walking around. I felt like a kid in a candy shop. I loved my visit.

Absolutely brilliant! This is a great spot to just wander and take in the art. 798 Art District is like a university campus or small village where every building is a gallery. The open areas are free space for sculptural art of the weird and wonderful kind. There's plenty of little cafes and bars to stop and relax for a bit, and people watch. A cab from Wangfujing cost about 60rmb and there are plenty of cabs cruising up and down the little streets of 798 so it's easy to get back into town. Allow plenty of time to walk around and discover 798. HIghly recommended for visitors to Beijing and a pleasant break from the countless historical sites.
Interesting place full of art shops, galleries and caffes. Looks more European than Chinese. You can can spend a few relaxing hours there enjoying art fusion.

Once the home of the North China Wireless Joint Equipment Factory, the 798 Art Zone is a vast compound built in the 50s that has been renovated to house dozens of galleries, design studios, art spaces, artists’ studios, ateliers, fashion houses, shops, restaurants, and bars. Today the 798 is also the epicenter of China’s street art scene. The 798 is like a coral reef where the art is as ephemeral as a school of tropical fish darting through a diverse ecosystem of throw-ups, tags, and graffiti as well as more elaborate art pieces like murals and sculptures. It's a must see!
Great place to wander around and see the latest of Chinese art. It's quite a big complex, with dozens of galleries and studios. Nice little cafes as well.

If you've ever been to Williamsburg in Brooklyn, it's basically that if you injected it into a late 19th century factory district that's been re-zoned for the specific purpose of attracting artsy people who do artsy things... but with less partying. Wall to wall art galleries and cafes interspersed with artisan jewelry and sunglass stores, unique and delicious restaurants, and lots of random stores that specialize in things like leather goods and Andy Warhol replicas galore will keep you strolling all afternoon! If you'd like a break from Beijing without leaving Beijing, go to 798. The only downsides: - Insufficient nightlife. I've been during the day and been at night, and despite it being the PERFECT place for nightclubs, on a Thursday night there were none to be found. Even the restaurants and cafes were all closed by 2200 (10pm) and we could only find one place that was open for cocktails. - It's off the beaten path. By that, I mean if you take the subway you're going to find yourself making a hefty walk, or needing to flag down a cab or call a DiDi to make it the rest of the way. Getting to it can be a pain. But it's worth the journey all in all. By the way, if you like cocktails, order a Lycee Martini (AKA Dragon's eye Martini) and you're in for a smooth ride into tipsy town you've ever encountered!
It's very nice place to express your art and culture experience, have a lot of gallery and artefact zone

Must try in Beijing if you love art. Do spend a day and explore all the alleys. You never know what you'll find. P.s. some galleries may be open/closed. They're either preparing for an exhibition or have finished one

This is more of a touristy store zone rather than an art zone. I didn't see much of art that was any impressive or inspiring. Almost Every gallery charges you for some "art". Beijing really needs more cultural and artistic depth!
Some of the best work I've seen a few years ago are no longer there, but it's still a great place to browse. Many food options. I'd give 5 stars if it isn't too commercialised now
Absolutely amazing district that showcases some very cool art pieces. Lots of different galleries to take a look at and enjoy.
A nice place to come for a day walk. Not many places open in the night so better visit before 7

One, if not the, highlight of my Beijing trip! Lots of different art styles and a unique vibe in the entire district. Give it at least an afternoon - I feel like I could've easily spent a few more hours there!
Fresh breath of contemporary art & culture in Beijing - must visit this to see a different side of the city full of hidden gems. Relaxed nice atmosphere, some great creative work to admire and buy.
A must when visiting Beijing. Great galleries and art stores, nice restaurants. The location is a bit remote and there should be better signaled as one arrives via public transportation.

Fantastic way to experience contemporary art in the center of Beijing. I liked the fact that it is a closed off area (from city traffic), which makes for a pleasant walk...Several blocks filled with lovely art galleries and coffee shops, a MUST see in Beijing

Very different from what you usually see in Beijing. Interesting to see this side, with it's street art and industrial looking buildings. There are a lot of small galleries, bars and restaurants. Definitely worth a visit.

Decided to visit reading previous comments. It is like little town, never ending. Lot of galleries, couple of monuments....nothing special to impress....would recommend visit just if you want to loose day out
Stayed here for a month - loved it! Best place in Beijing. Can't wait to come back. I love living in 798 Art District with all the street food and shops. Couldn't get enough of it!

One of the must visit place in Beijing. Lots of indie designer shop, product, and gallery. Some of the gallery is free. But the traffic awful, and felt unsafe when walking. Couldn't understand why people drive into the area.
great place, amazing exhibitions and artists, seeing around is lovely and chilling
Visit here in 2013 and can't wait to go back. This is one of my most favorite places when I visited Beijing. I love art and the art here is so unique. Can't wait to go back.
great examples of work produced by local artists.....as well as some great places to eat....and most importantly there are some good cafes offering good coffee.
Amazing place. A lot of art galeries and stores nested in an old factory. Some very interesting pieces of art.
You can spend a beautiful evening in art zone, enjoying art in several galleries for free and also Cafe's
When I was there it was a bit too calm. The area is nice, but it was not as expected (too empty, a bit too much souvenir shops)
Very interesting. Surprised to find such an interesting art location near Beijing. A wide variety of indoor and outdoor exhibits.
Interesting place to visit and walk around on a weekday afternoon. Lots of art pieces (eg. sculptures) placed around in the district.
beautiful place to wander and explore. art lovers can plan to spend a whole day here.
Very cool District. Regulated traffic, which makes it appear much more calm compared to the rest of Beijing. Industrial design.
This place is always full of tourists. I enjoyed the Russian festival. Lots of fun!
This is a place that you can hangout with your friends, visiting lots of fun shops, studios, purchasing unique stuff.
Best place in Beijing for modern art and discovering interesting and less seen side of the city
Great before 2006 when it changed to an commercial art circus and tourist hotspot in 2008. But still special and worth to see.
A must visit place for art loving people... A place to experience various dimensions of art...
Still a fantastic modern art zone, but has become more standard and a.bit boring.

Es un distrito de arte contemporáneo en Pekín lleno de galerías, cafés y murales coloridos. Aunque tiene un ambiente creativo interesante, esperaba que fuera más sorprendente. Algunas zonas resultan más comerciales que artísticas, aunque sigue siendo un paseo curioso para descubrir también el lado moderno de la ciudad.

Die 798 Art Zone ist ein echtes Highlight und zeigt die moderne, kreative Seite Pekings. Die Vielfalt an Ausstellungen – von zeitgenössischer chinesischer Kunst bis hin zu internationalen Werken – ist beeindruckend. Die Atmosphäre ist inspirierend und lebendig, das gesamte Areal ist liebevoll gestaltet und lädt zum Entdecken und Verweilen ein. Besonders schön war auch unser Besuch in einem charmanten Lokal vor Ort, in dem wir ausgesprochen gut gegessen haben – besonders die Peking Ente und ein köstliches Auberginengericht sind uns in Erinnerung geblieben (leider wissen wir den Namen des Restaurants nicht mehr). Das Areal ist frei zugänglich und kann ohne Ticket besucht werden, was den spontanen Besuch besonders angenehm macht.
この地区のギャラリーは大体10時オープンのところが多いです。 9時にオープンするギャラリーもありますが、私が行ったときは9時を過ぎてもしまっていました。 お昼過ぎくらいに行くのがちょうど良いかと思います。
可以徒步走進798藝術區的街區，感受藝文活動和潮流商品配件，也能逛逛書店，參觀美術展覽，想喝咖啡還是吃飯也都有。如果在北京有半天停留的時間，喔悠閒來走走很不錯，
北京798藝術區充滿前衛與創意，是工業遺跡與當代藝術完美融合的空間。漫步其間，不時可見塗鴉牆、裝置藝術與設計小店，令人目不暇給。無論是藝術愛好者還是想找個有氛圍的地方拍照、喝咖啡，都能在這裡找到驚喜。
Quartiere autentico di Pechino non turistico. Dove i giovani studenti cinesi trascorrono il loro tempi e si incontrano tra amici in un posto pieno di arte contemporanea.
Wir haben das Viertel am Abend im Rahmen eines kurzen Layovers besucht, da es vom Flughafen aus gut mit dem Taxi zu erreichen ist. Es hat sich mehr als gelohnt! Super kreativ und schön gestaltet.

Mwah aardig als tijd vulling maar geen must see.... Veel panden worden nog verbouwd. Grote galleries 30 tot 80 RMB toegangsprijs. Fuijsu foto gallery was gratis en wel mooie fotos om te bekijken. Totale duur dat wij er waren 1,5 uur.
798廢棄工廠有許多磚砌建築和高大的煙囪，工廠建築變為藝術工作室、展覽中心及餐廳 磚牆塗鴉令人驚艷的街頭藝術，文創手工設計也看得到，滿滿的文青感 網路上說場地大到可以逛兩天 我們只去一個小時的景點 然後又下點小雨，然後我又迷失在廢墟巷弄裡╮(￣▽￣"")╭ 問了當地的居民和新來的警衛，皆不知道北處廣場的五牛圖，幸好騎著電動摩托車巡查的老警衛稍上我繞了半圈，才來得及趕到集合地點 謝謝北京人的熱心
Area industriale e ferroviaria riconvertita in i affiscinamte polo culturale: perdetevi tra le stradine e cercate quanto di meglio possa essere vicino ai vostri interessi artistici

Un espacio abierto con muchas galerías de arte dónde puedes ver un sin fin de expresiónes artísticas en su mayoría contemporáneas. Cuenta con algunos restaurantes distribuidos en a lo largo del lugar donde te puedes sentar a disfrutar y pasar un rato chill. Encontraras tiendas que venden obras, cuadros , figuras , ropa realmente muy variado. El ambiente es espectacular porque no es el tipico lugar familiar entonces no está tan lleno. Yo fui en agosto temporada alta y fue uno de los pocos lugares que más me agradó visitar en Beijing porque no estaba atestado de personas. Recomiendo ir en la tarde ya entrando el atardecer 5 pm aprox para poder tener un climas un poco la fresco. Definitivamente pienso ir cada vez que vaya a Beijing.
Aan te bevelen voor even een andere highlight dan de gebruikelijke in Beijing. Leuke winkels lekkere sfeer.

1952년에 만들어진 중국 현대 공업의 발원지로 냉전시대에는 소련과 독일의 기술로 무기를 만들던 공장이 있었다고 합니다. 이후 공장들이 자리를 옮기면서 2002년부터 예술가들이 모여들어 버려진 공장 폐허를 이용하여 갤러리와 작업실 등을 만들기 시작하면서 지금의 예술구가 시작 되었다고 하며, 지금은 북경 최대의 예술 거리가 되었다고 합니다. 아름다운 건물들과 독특한 조각상들 그리고 자유로움 예술의 분위기로 가득한 거리가 가는 곳 마다 발걸음을 멈추게 합니다. 천천히 거닐며 거리의 조형물들을 감상하고 차분하게 차를 마시며 쉴 수 있는 거리입니다.
週一來的，有比較多展都關著，而且走了很多路，其實只是走了整個大區的幾分之一😆 代表還有很多沒有逛到。裡面有很多小咖啡館、餐廳，還有不少手作、純手工藝製作的作品，滿滿的文青感。很舒服的一個下午！

Las fábricas industriales y almacenes de la era comunista, abandonados gradualmente en la década de 1990, fueron tomados por creativos, artistas, diseñadores, escultores y pintores que trasladaron aquí sus talleres debido al bajo precio de los alquileres. Con el tiempo, esta zona de fábricas estilo Bauhaus, grandes chimeneas y tuberías oxidadas, se transformó con la apertura de galerías, salas de exposiciones, tiendas, estudios de diseño y arquitectura, bares y restaurantes vanguardistas, dando color y vida a los restos de las fábricas. Este distrito del arte, el más grande e influyente de China, es una visita imprescindible para conocer lo último en diseño y comprender la cultura china contemporánea.

798 befindet sich auf einem ehemaligen Fabrikgelände. Viele Backsteingebäude und Schornsteine zeugen von dieser Zeit. Der rote Backstein bildet eine wunderbare Kulisse für die vielen ausgestellten Skulpturen, aber auch Fashion Shootings finden hier statt. Das Gelände ist sehr weitläufig, aber Cafés und Restaurants laden zum Pausieren ein. Wer alle der vielen Gallerien besuchen möchte muss sich sicher einen ganzen Tag dafür Zeit nehmen. Kleine Läden mit Kunsthandwerk, Designer Mode, Töpferware, Souvenirs und Portrait Zeichner runden das Angebot auf dem Gelände ab.

Sehr netter Kunstbezirk, welcher leider nicht mehr ganz so überzeugen kann wie vor 5 Jahren. Damals wesentlich interessanter und wesentlich mehr Interaktive Möglichkeiten. Zudem sind die Cafés und Restaurants, die früher bereits teurer waren, nun unverhältnismäßig teuer. Für einen Kurzausflug trotzdem noch ganz nett.
昔の軍事工場を改装した美術館、ギャラリー、カフェ、レストランなどが集中する地域。建物の外にも昔のスローガンと現代の彫刻が混在しており歩いていて面白い。秋には芸術祭が開かれ、入れる建物が増える。 至る所に置いてあるオブジェは頻繁に移動したり、入れ替わったりする。ここで見かけなくなったオブジェが街のデパート内にあったりして驚くことがある。 798芸術区を東へ抜けると『751 D-PARK』がある。

798 Art Zone is een unieke en boeiende artistieke wijk in Beijing. Het staat bekend als de thuisbasis van vele galerieën, studio's en tentoonstellingsruimten van enkele van de meest innovatieve en opkomende kunstenaars. Het is de perfecte plek om te verkennen en te genieten van een breed scala aan artistieke werken, van fotografie en beeldhouwkunst tot schilderkunst, muurschilderingen en installaties. Naast de vele galeries vind je er ook hippe cafés, restaurants en boetieks, waardoor het een levendige en bruisende bestemming is voor zowel de lokale bevolking als toeristen. Als je op zoek bent naar een culturele ervaring in Beijing, is 798 Art Zone absoluut een bezoek waard.

798艺术区位于朝阳区东北，是老厂房改造的创意园区。 现在已是北京的新地标和文艺青年聚集地，驻扎了很多画廊、展馆和独立艺术家，建筑也都新锐时尚，设计感十足，还有不少特色店铺，是年轻人感受文艺气息的妙处。游玩时间798艺术区的范围较大，大约长宽都在1公里左右，各个画廊和展览馆、艺术中心等分布在一座座改造的厂房内，沿路步行一一参观即可。798的展馆、艺术中心等营业时间大致在10:00-18:00左右，每周一基本都会闭馆，注意选好时间前来。一般游客在这里简单观光大约半天即可，如果认真观看展览、艺术品等则需要一天时间。观展在798逛街，主要便是感受这里的艺术气息，而观展就是最主要的内容。

里面有各种展，超赞，但是吃饭的地不是很给力。
藝術畫廊匯集之地，一次能逛到好多好作品

reviews.text: 直接五星好評，因為這是文化生長的地方、可以玩一整天
北京不擁擠的經典，場地大可以慢慢逛！
文青打卡点，有些舊厰房遺物
哈哈哈，798艺术区感觉没那么有艺术，大几十一碗的麻辣烫价格倒是非常有现代行为艺术～
展馆算不上特别多，也都是些小展览，除了展馆以外没有什么好看的。
和朋友去过， 里面的废弃的火车挺有感觉的， 很多模特在那里拍照片
说实话，798可逛的实在不多，也就玩弄一些文革时代的老回忆，美其名曰文艺。
798有很多portal，有很多工作室和创意工坊 目测portal应该还可以再密集一些再多一些

到北京一定要去798，最近一次去看艾未未的艺术展。
可以逛逛，照相不錯，看看創業小物
藝術風格的商店街，很不錯！
분위기 좋은 펍이나 카페도 많고 구석구석 느낌있는 곳.
是一个很有特色的地方，艺术生们的最爱呀！
생각보다 꿀잼. 가신다면 많은 가게들 구경하시는 게 가장 좋은 구경방법인 듯.
